description: Twenty-one curated teaching cards, not twenty-one unique source documents or puzzles. Distinguish sourced evidence from curator inference. Not a training-rights-cleared corpus.

cards.title: Flag mashups lead to geographic lines
cards.documented_evidence: An official solution uses mashups of national flags and a map/geodesic construction.
cards.curator_inference: Consider shifting from flag imagery to relationships among countries and geographic paths.
cards.contrast_test: A proposed geographic rule should predict intersections or destinations for cases not used to tune it.
cards.limitations: Presented solve, not a dated human discovery history.

cards.title: Word lengths correspond to diagram diagonals
cards.documented_evidence: The solution relates clue-word lengths to the lengths of sloping diagonals of a triangular chalice grid.
cards.curator_inference: Treat visible grid capacity and length distribution as mutual constraints, not decorative structure.
cards.contrast_test: Try placing independently solved clue words and check overlapping letters without discretionary adjustments.
cards.limitations: An official explanation; initial inference chronology is unknown.

cards.title: Colored stems specify an interleaving operation
cards.documented_evidence: The solution uses the chalice's colored stem bands to determine how extracted colored letters are riffled.
cards.curator_inference: Read a repeated color pattern as an operation/order rather than additional data.
cards.contrast_test: Freeze the band-to-letter mapping and check it across multiple chalices.
cards.limitations: Same puzzle/source as another card; not independent case.

cards.title: Pictures as terminal clues in a recursive tree
cards.documented_evidence: The official solution describes a rooted tree: images at leaves are identified and reparsed into crossword-style clues, which recursively combine.
cards.curator_inference: Reframe the diagram as a computation graph where each node's output becomes a parent clue.
cards.contrast_test: Predict an unworked internal node from its children, then check propagation toward the root.
cards.limitations: This teaches the published mechanism, not a firsthand solver breakthrough.

cards.title: Meaning depends on reparsing word boundaries
cards.documented_evidence: The solution illustrates pictures for NO and THIGH being reparsed as NOT HIGH, a clue for LOW.
cards.curator_inference: Words can be meaningful *after* boundary changes; surface word segmentation is not fixed.
cards.contrast_test: Test if several sibling nodes yield valid downstream clues under the same reparsing rule.
cards.limitations: Do not treat arbitrary phrase punning as a proof of intended mechanism.

cards.title: Flavor geometry motivates an unusual crossword shape
cards.documented_evidence: The official solution links a cut Guadeloupe coin with an irregularly shaped gridless crossword.
cards.curator_inference: Treat a reference object's shape as a constraint on layout and manipulation.
cards.contrast_test: Before reading extracted words, check whether the proposed shape accounts for the full grid structure.
cards.limitations: Historical reference and shape are supplied by source; creative motivation is curator inference.

cards.title: Testimony paragraphs form an interleaved timeline
cards.documented_evidence: The official solution combines testimony paragraphs by Clue-character turn order to reconstruct events.
cards.curator_inference: Reframe independent narratives as interleaved observations of one evolving state.
cards.contrast_test: Use ordering to deduce a location at an unseen turn, and reject sequences violating other testimony.
cards.limitations: Full-solution chronology is not necessarily solver discovery chronology.

cards.title: A phrase changes role from answer to instruction for next puzzle
cards.documented_evidence: The final solution uses a Sherlock Holmes reference and an enumeration to obtain SCARLET IN A STUDY.
cards.curator_inference: Treat a previous answer as input to a second-stage transformation, not only as an endpoint.
cards.contrast_test: Verify the reinterpreted phrase matches the requested answer format and prior constraints.
cards.limitations: Multi-stage hunt conventions may not transfer to standalone tasks.

cards.title: Minimal changes can reveal a hidden distance rule
cards.documented_evidence: The official solution includes a practice interaction for inferring a hidden rule, such as testing changed letters.
cards.curator_inference: Use isolated perturbations to infer an oracle's mechanism from controlled differences.
cards.contrast_test: Design paired inputs that separate Hamming, edit, vowel-class and position-sensitive proposals.
cards.limitations: The official solution is publicly referenced; rule-detail reconstruction should be checked against source before citing narrowly.

cards.title: Practice examples are a calibration channel
cards.documented_evidence: An official guide points solvers to a practice round rather than brute-forcing the main puzzle at once.
cards.curator_inference: Reassign a small example to calibration/teaching instead of treating it as another full-sized clue.
cards.contrast_test: Infer a rule on a limited example; lock it before applying to a new instance.
cards.limitations: Same underlying puzzle as official-09; do not count twice as a unique puzzle.

cards.title: Grid edges eliminate impossible tile orientations
cards.reported_discovery_trigger: Playing Net by hand and noticing forced rotations.
cards.documented_evidence: Tatham recounts deriving local rules: pieces near borders lose orientations that point connections outside the grid.
cards.curator_inference: Begin with hard boundaries before global search.
cards.contrast_test: Enumerate tile orientations around a grid edge and exclude those inconsistent with the boundary.
cards.limitations: Described historical solver-design reasoning, not an arbitrary hunt solution.

cards.title: Track edge states independently from tile states
cards.reported_discovery_trigger: Tile-only constraints left useful edge-level information implicit.
cards.documented_evidence: Tatham describes recording definitely connected or disconnected edges even while tile orientation remains uncertain.
cards.curator_inference: Change the model's primitive from only tile states to edges with partial certainty.
cards.contrast_test: Find a position whose tile is ambiguous but adjacent edge can be proved fixed.
cards.limitations: Several cards are from the same historical account.

cards.title: Known connectivity exposes forbidden loops
cards.reported_discovery_trigger: Local propagation alone did not capture loop constraints.
cards.documented_evidence: The account describes using a disjoint-set structure for currently known connected squares and rejecting edges forming a loop.
cards.curator_inference: Add global graph connectivity invariants to local orientation logic.
cards.contrast_test: If endpoints already share a connected path, test whether adding a candidate edge creates an illegal cycle.
cards.limitations: Works for this puzzle's tree-like connectedness requirement, not every network puzzle.

cards.title: Generalize specific dead ends into a reachability bound
cards.reported_discovery_trigger: Repeated special-case dead-end deductions suggested a general invariant.
cards.documented_evidence: Tatham describes moving from special cases involving endpoints to per-edge maximum reachable square bounds.
cards.curator_inference: Turn a collection of exceptions into one general recurrence over candidate orientations.
cards.contrast_test: Apply the same bound to a tiny grid, a large grid and an adversarial branch.
cards.limitations: A bound's implementation may differ from human informal reasoning.

cards.title: Region parity constrains possible connections
cards.reported_discovery_trigger: A human deduction persisted beyond the implemented search representation.
cards.documented_evidence: Tatham identifies a region-degree parity technique he uses manually but had not implemented in the solver described there.
cards.curator_inference: A region boundary can carry a mod-2 invariant even when individual edges remain unknown.
cards.contrast_test: Count degrees inside a boundary and compare against candidate crossing parity.
cards.limitations: The source explicitly discusses this as not yet implemented in that solver.

cards.title: Test whether a generated board is logically solvable
cards.reported_discovery_trigger: The design question is how to guarantee no-guess play.
cards.documented_evidence: Tatham explains a Mines generator that avoids releasing boards that require guessing, discussing why a simple forbidden-pattern characterization may not suffice.
cards.curator_inference: Use an actual solving procedure to test a proposed construction rather than rely on a vague appearance of solvability.
cards.contrast_test: Compare an easy board with a board whose next move cannot be forced under the specified deduction system.
cards.limitations: A generator's solvability standard depends on the precise permitted inference rules.

cards.title: A physical model changes what a cube net means
cards.reported_discovery_trigger: The visible cube nets prompted attempts to fold them physically.
cards.documented_evidence: A firsthand bENDs account describes working with printed cube nets and writing code to investigate their geometry.
cards.curator_inference: Shift from 2-D marks to a 3-D assembled object before attempting extraction.
cards.contrast_test: Check whether folds align faces and symbols in ways that planar interpretation cannot explain.
cards.limitations: The retrospective notes its own incompleteness; it does not establish that every subcheck was verified.

cards.title: Fuse two loop puzzle genres to induce new rules
cards.documented_evidence: Evan Chen recounts combining Masyu and Moon-or-Sun puzzle ideas in a hunt round.
cards.curator_inference: Use shared structural features of two known genres to create a new system whose rules must be inferred.
cards.contrast_test: Ask whether the proposed hybrid rule creates a solvable and meaningfully constrained example.
cards.limitations: Author perspective: explains design decisions, not a record of individual testsolver thought.

cards.title: A number can confirm rule inference instead of solving the grid
cards.documented_evidence: The author notes that counts of black/white pearls, moons and suns were intended to confirm the conjectured rule set.
cards.curator_inference: Treat a number as a checksum/calibration rather than a direct move.
cards.contrast_test: Try a second rule interpretation and see whether the fixed counts reject it.
cards.limitations: Do not infer that every number is a checksum.

cards.title: Puzzle construction can add explicit stopping conditions
cards.documented_evidence: The constructors say they introduced pictured terminal nodes so recursive clueing would not continue indefinitely, then revised a branch after testsolving.
cards.curator_inference: Treat a peculiar clue form as a boundary/termination rule that might prevent uncontrolled recursion.
cards.contrast_test: Identify a finite measure that decreases toward terminal nodes and check all paths.
cards.limitations: Constructor intent is documented; a solver might not recognize it initially.

cards.title: Testsolving revealed a shortcut through a meta
cards.documented_evidence: The authors report splitting the meta after a testsolver guessed the later reference without performing the intended intermediary.
cards.curator_inference: A very direct answer may bypass an intended mechanism; distinguish correct output from evidence of mechanism.
cards.contrast_test: Check whether a candidate answer accounts for feeder mechanics or merely predicts the final phrase.
cards.limitations: An unintended shortcut can still yield a correct submitted answer; do not reject solely on aesthetics.
